items.title: HoYoverse creature collector Honkai: Nexus Anima is launching Spring 2027, Final Closed Beta begins this month
items.summary: HoYoverse have announced the release date, and final beta date, for their next big online game, Honkai: Nexus Anima.
items.content:
HoYoverse , makers of popular live service gacha games such as Genshin Impact and Zenless Zone Zero , have announced the release date, and final beta date, for their next big online game, Honkai: Nexus Anima . Honkai Nexus Anima will launch in Spring 2027 on PC and mobile devices.

The Final Closed Beta for Honkai: Nexus Anima will begin on November 25. Players can sign up now for a chance to play — though all progress and data will be wiped when the test ends. Sign up for the beta ends November 22.

Honkai: Nexus Anima is HoYoverse’s take on the creature collector genre (aka Pokémon , Palworld , etc). Players take on the role of Animasters and explore across multiple worlds, called Planes. Each Plane is home to powerful creatures called Anima.

The primary gameplay loop involves exploring each Plane, and finding and recruiting Anima, as well as their signature trainers, called Eidos.

In terms of gacha, the Anima are the primary gacha targets, while the Eidos represent their signature weapons.

Combat in every HoYoverse game is different, and Nexus Anima is no exception. The real-time combat is inspired by autobattlers/autochess. A team of Anima automatically attacks and moves on a grid-based battlefield, while players unleash active, targeted abilities from their Eidos.

Between exploring and battling, players can chill at their personal RV home, where they can decorate and interact with their Anima.

Given that Honkai: Nexus Anima has the same series name as Honkai: Stair Rail (and the fifth in the Honkai series overall), players can expect some crossover with the RPG series, including the appearance of Star Rail’s Blade as an Eidos trainer.

HoYoverse is known for their incredible high production value, anime art designs, professional voice acting, and constant flow of major content updates. The studio is also known for producing gacha games , live service online games that promote random in-game items and characters that players can purchase with real money. The gacha game system is often criticized as a form of unregulated gambling.

Honkai: Nexus Anima will release in Spring 2027 on PC and iOS and Android mobile platforms.

items.title: Face the Leviathan in the Honkai: Star Rail 4.7 Trailer!
Honkai: Star Rail to Release Version 4.7 Update on November 11
items.summary: HoYoverse announced on November 2 that Version 4.7, titled "Now, Lay Laughter to All Stars," will be released for Honkai: Star Rail on November 11.
items.content:
Korean (한국어) KO Add us on ⓒ HoYoverse HoYoverse announced on November 2 that Version 4.7, titled "Now, Lay Laughter to All Stars," will be released for Honkai: Star Rail on November 11. This update introduces the limited 5-star character "Aeon★Aha" and the new character development system "EX-Eidolon," while the permanent content "Currency Wars" enters Season 2.

Joining as a playable character, "Aeon★Aha" is a character on the Path of Elation. They unlock new combat abilities for characters of the same Path within the party and accelerate the combat tempo of Elation skills during "Aha Time". When "Willpower," accumulated based on party members' actions, reaches a certain threshold, Aeon★Aha unleashes an Ultimate that deals Elation DMG to all enemies. Powered by the authority of an Aeon, ally attacks can also directly reduce enemies' max HP.

Character reruns will be split into the first and second halves of the version. The first half features limited 5-star characters "Silver Wolf LV.999," "Sparxie," and "Yao Guang," while the second half features "Acheron," "Dan Heng • Imbibitor Lunae," and "Jing Yuan". The "EX-Eidolon" system, which unlocks new additional skills for designated characters, will first apply combat buffs to "Acheron," "Dan Heng • Imbibitor Lunae," and "Jing Yuan".

In this story, the Trailblazer teams up with Aha, the Aeon of Elation, to face the ancient beast "Voracity". As "Voracity," which had been sealed in the "Illusion Moon Game" for thousands of Amber Eras, awakens, Aha executes the "Voracity Hunt" plan to stop the monster before its power fully recovers. To this end, Aha gathers eight petitioners and holds the "Final Illusion Moon Game" aboard the giant airship "Starfroster". This performance marks the final show that will decide the fate of "Planarcadia".

The permanent content "Currency Wars" will be reorganized for Season 2, "Bizarre Voyage in the Painting". Version events include "The Fluffy Express Movie: Bustling Kitchen," where players run a dessert shop with Aha, and the combat event "Starpeace Festival: Path of the Star". In "Fantasy Showtime," players can earn rewards such as the limited outfit "Starry Lottery" for Aeon★Aha.

On the update day of November 11, the short animated film "A Cheerful Funeral Under the Moonlight" will be released. The new song "Creation from Nothingness," which brings the story of "Planarcadia" to a grand conclusion, will also be unveiled.

Honkai: Star Rail will also participate in G-STAR 2026, which will be held from November 19 to 22 at BEXCO in Busan. A variety of stage programs will be hosted on-site.

items.title: Manage a Dessert Shop with an Actual God in Honkai: Star Rail's Climactic PS5 Update
items.content:
If you’re a regular of HoYoverse’s turn-based RPG Honkai: Star Rail , then you’ll probably have been waiting for 5-Star character Aha’s arrival, as part of v4.7 on 11th November.

The anticipated Aeon is effectively a god, bringing outrageous buffs to all characters on the path of Elation. She’s going to be essential if you’ve been pulling for any of the characters featured in the Planarcadia arc, like Sparxie and Silver Wolf Lv 999.

Her introduction to the gacha pool will coincide with a climactic conclusion to the current storyline.

I must admit, I’m a little relieved to hear that because while I’ve undoubtedly enjoyed the vibes of this new planet, the dev’s lore-heavy writing is losing me a lot lately. I personally find it difficult to keep up with the constant proper nouns.

Other activities in this update include a dessert shop management minigame that looks like a ton of fun, as well as new rules and content for the auto-chess inspired endgame mode, Currency Wars.

As mentioned, all of this new content will debut on 11th November, which is the same day as NTE’s new update goes live . That’s a lot of gacha game to get through before GTA 6 .

Why Honkai: Star Rail players talk quitting the game
items.summary: Honkai: Star Rail players and creators are debating whether to quit amid complaints about power creep, endgame design, events and story presentation.
items.content:
A wave of Reddit posts and YouTube videos about quitting Hoyoverse ‘s Honkai: Star Rail has put long-running complaints over power creep, endgame design and story presentation back at the centre of the game’s community debate.

The discussion does not establish that Star Rail is facing a measurable player exodus. The sources reviewed offer no player-count data. What they do show is a recurring concern from active and former players: the game can demand continued investment while giving some of them fewer reasons to log in.

YouTuber Pixel Tree , who said he had not played Star Rail for some time, argued that the current criticism was more notable because it was coming from the game’s own community rather than rival fandoms. He said seeing regular Star Rail creators express frustration suggested there was a genuine issue behind the wider social media debate.

Power creep is one of the complaints that appears most consistently across the Reddit post and creator videos. Players argue that the gap between older and newer characters has grown enough to change how they approach pulling, building and spending on units.

Read more: Hoyoverse announces Genshin Impact 7.1 Special Program date

GachaNekoVT , who said he still plays Star Rail, argued that the problem goes beyond new characters simply being stronger. Players may begin wondering how long a newly acquired character will remain useful before another unit performs the same role more effectively.

That can also make spending harder to justify. Building a character can take weeks or months, while obtaining higher Eidolons or signature Light Cones can require further investment. The concern is that the value of that investment may decline much faster than players expect.

Similar complaints in the material point to newer characters replacing older ones with comparable but stronger kits, widening the perceived gap between generations of units.

Endgame design has intensified that frustration. Players criticised rising enemy health and mechanics that favour particular character archetypes or team compositions. The Reddit author described the meta as increasingly punishing for players who want to continue using older characters.

Read more: Genshin Impact 7.0: Are Flins and Ineffa worth pulling?

Kekvin agreed that recent bosses and endgame modes can restrict viable teams, although he noted that power creep itself is hardly new to Star Rail. His criticism focused more on how newer encounters can turn difficulty into a question of which characters a player owns rather than how they use them.

The Reddit post from DependentNo1079 described Planarcadia as a story that was not necessarily bad but had failed to meet expectations. Its author pointed to repetitive animations, lengthy dialogue and presentation that can struggle to make major story moments feel distinct.

Pixel Tree discussed similar complaints, including repeated character poses, reused models and limited animation. The material also highlights the game’s frequent reliance on text screens during story sequences, an approach that has become a recurring joke within the community.

GachaNekoVT raised a different problem with the writing itself. He praised Star Rail’s characters and music but argued that recent stories can become difficult to follow because of the volume of lore, terminology and exposition.

MAPPA, HoYoverse Release 'Animation Concept Trailer' for Honkai: Star Rail Game (Updated)
items.content:
HoYoverse revealed during a livestream for its Honkai: Star Rail game on Friday that it and MAPPA have co-produced an "animation concept trailer" for the game. The trailer, viewable below, is titled "Death in the Afternoon."

Yuzuru Tachikawa ( Mob Psycho 100 , Death Parade director) directed the trailer and Kayoko Ishikawa ( Sarazanmai , ZENSHU. ) was the character designer. The end of the above video features the words " MAPPA Honkai: Star Rail Animation A New Story Awaits."

The HoYoverse staff had introduced the video in the livestream as a "mysterious collaboration project." HoYoverse's press release about the livestream announcements stated that at the end of the livestream, "...the original animation project co-produced by HoYoverse and MAPPA premiered its concept trailer, 'Death in the Afternoon.' Please look forward to the continuing cosmic adventures!"

The livestream and HoYoverse's press release did not give any further details. It is currently unclear if the "original animation project" is the above trailer, or if the collaboration will include other works.

Update: ANN reached out to HoYoverse for clarification, and the company provided the following response:

HoYoverse launched its Honkai: Star Rail game for PC and mobile in April 2023, and then for PlayStation 5 in October 2023. The game has exceeded 150 million total downloads across all platforms.

The game will launch its Version 4.2 patch on April 22. The patch will celebrate the game's third anniversary.

HoYoverse's earlier game Genshin Impact launched a "long-term collaboration project" with ufotable in 2022. The project is still in production.

Sources: Press release, Honkai: Star Rail game's YouTube channel ( link 2 )

items.title: Honkai: Star Rail 4.0 impressions
items.content:
I'll admit, I recently burned out on Honkai: Star Rail. Upon hearing the news that 3.8 would be the lengthiest patch yet and with content more sparse than ever before, I decided to take a break for the first time since I started playing all the way back in 1.0. The entire Amphoreus saga left me feeling drained; I thoroughly enjoyed 3.0-3.4 as excellent set-up chapters, but felt lost as the plot became a labyrinth of hidden motivations, layered twists, hours of exposition, and endless proper nouns. When looking at the story as a whole, I love the characters (Aglaea and Anaxa in particular) and the rich history of the world within the Scepter, but the later patches often felt like studying for a needlessly convoluted test. I understood the gist of what was happening, but I won't lie to you and say I could describe to you in detail what Cyrene's deal is or how Evernight fits into everything.

All that's to say: I was looking forward to the Astral Express crew taking a well-earned vacation to Planarcadia, the planet of Elation. Despite two of the game's four current versions ostensibly beginning with Akivili's disciples deciding that they need a break from the backbreaking work of saving the universe, neither has resulted in our trailblazers seeing much downtime. Unlike previous excursions, it's all hands on deck: everyone gets off at this stop (save for Black Swan's incredibly hasty and unfortunate exit prior to departure). It's fun to see the entire main cast get involved, none more welcome than Himeko — up until now, the only character trait I could've told you about her was that she's terrible at making coffee. Getting some elaboration on her backstory and giving her a personality outside of "Express mom" is long overdue.

The Trailblazer and March 7th begin their Planarcadian getaway with a suitably devious greeting by none other than our old pal Sparkle. We're given a tour of the vibrant, totally-not-Japanese-inspired streets, crawling with humans living in tentative harmony with totally-not-Penaconian-memetic-entities known as imagenae. Here, we catch a glimpse of what I hope will become one of Planarcadia's core themes: gentrification and the plight of capitalism, with a side of anti-imperialism (all perpetrated by the IPC, of course). It's bold, though, and I worry that future patches will keep these criticisms in the background rather than highlight them as Planarcadia's core issues. I would love so much for little nuggets of lore to be elaborated upon, ones that suggest a more serious political history than Aha would have you believe: what did the imagenae do before the IPC forced them to integrate into society? Were they not allowed to work at all? Were they marginalized and seen as second-class citizens? Is the Department of Aberration Defense an inherently evil organization left to determine on their own which imagenae deserve their continued existence and which do not? Is Kuchiba so hot that it doesn't even matter?

This brings us to the Synwish Syndicate, a gang formerly designed to be a respite for imagenae that feel rejected elsewhere, now, due to IPC intervention, a gang that largely exists to enable monetary gain by questionable means. Here at the syndicate's headquarters, the plot quickly begins to balloon into what feels like a collection of introductions for what's to come. We have Pearl's cold and calculating grip on the planet, Himeko and her confounding family history, the potential return of the Herald of Death, the Stellaron Hunters' unknown involvement in the Phantasmoon Games, Sunday's inadvertent entry into the Games, Evanescia's whole...thing, and Yao Guang's bottomless supply of divinations. What's most shocking is that the patch still manages to pull off a fun (if bloated) self-contained story, adding layers to one of HSR's most inscrutable characters and ending things with one of the game's best low-stakes twists.

I'm no Xianzhou Arbiter-General, but I can pretty easily peer into the future and divine a prophecy for Honkai: Star Rail: each new patch will introduce and/or discuss at length a new prophecy that cryptically divulges the fate of a character and/or planet and/or simulation masquerading as a planet. It's hard to pinpoint the moment a theme becomes a crutch, but I think HSR passed that moment long ago. In this patch, we have not one, not two, but three central characters that are defined by their relationship with prophecy and prediction — Yao Guang, Pearl, and the perennial mystery that is Elio and his script. So many in-game conversations devolve into the interpretation of prophecy, and frankly, it's becoming exhausting. We went through an entire version in which each Chrysos Heir had a poetically vague predetermined fate, and before that (and in 3.8's ret-con-y confusion) we had Sparkle's ambiguous "three deaths" for Firefly.

If this were a wholesale replacement for well-executed foreshadowing, we would have a far bigger issue. It's obvious, though, that the writing team knows how to tell a story sans-prophecy, evident in Sparkle's character-driven narrative in this very patch. Sparxie being the "true" Sparkle (as much as old Sparkle is also the "true" Sparkle) is teased so perfectly; the reveal is obvious in retrospect while being difficult to predict with the given information. It's consistently groan-inducing to see this writing cheat code being used ad nauseam within a story that could function better without it. I hope I'll be proven wrong and the game will subvert the words of its murky prophets, leaving me with egg on my face come the conclusion of this leg of the Express' journey.

4.0 is a promising new beginning, and has at the very least brought me back in terms of its story. Though there is an abundance of new proper nouns to memorize and a bevy of new and returning cast members to keep track of, the patch still takes on a welcome return to simplicity and levity (save for the shocking tonal shift right at the end, RIP the Synwish Syndicate Feb. 2026 - Feb. 2026). As long as things don't get too bogged down in extensive metaphors and tiresome exposition, I'm hopeful that Planarcadia can become the most focused version of HSR we've seen so far.
